opti-1: Sunbeams shine down over the Gulf.
opti-2: Every beam is a straight line.
opti-3: Something looks strange at this Florida lake…
opti-4: Flip it over! It was the trees' reflection in still water.
opti-5: A dark road soaks up sunlight and gets hot.
opti-6: Rubbing makes heat too. These race car brakes glow!
opti-8: How do light and heat energy interact with different materials?
28-02-welcome: Our film starts with sunbeams over the Gulf. First, inspect a giant glass object from a Florida museum.
28-02-lesson: Today you're a light scientist. Follow a sunbeam, test two shirts, then trace one beam through four materials.
28-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
28-02-assign: Time to show what you learned. Fill in the light chart, then draw where the light goes.
how-28-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the glass, then tap three things you notice.
how-28-02-compare: Put the flashlight under one tray and the sunshine under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Run the test. Then swap.
how-28-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing step: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-28-02-det: Pick three files, one at a time. Tap a clue, then name what is happening. Predict if it gets hotter or stays cooler, and watch the place appear.
how-28-02-partc: Draw a diagram showing a flashlight shining on three different surfaces: a mirror, white paper, and black paper. Use arrows to show where the light goes for each surface. Label whether each surface mainly reflects or absorbs the light.
